b.answer:
Worked example: Glow Studio, a fictional hair salon in Enugu.

PillarFed by
Style of the weekPrice list sheet
Behind the chairOwner's phone photos in a Drive folder (staff agreed)
Client transformationsBefore-and-after photos with written permission
Hair-care tipsThe stylists' tips list
Offers and datesSeasons sheet: Christmas, Easter, back-to-school

Cadence: Instagram 4 a week, Facebook 3, TikTok 2 videos, WhatsApp broadcast at most once a week to clients who opted in.

Brand voice (summary of the one page): warm, confident, Nigerian English; first names only with permission; up to two emoji; never say "cheapest in Enugu", never promise hair growth or health results; prices only from the sheet.

Week 1 of the four-week calendar

Weeks 2 to 4 follow the same pattern, with ideas the AI drafted and the owner trimmed. Two AI ideas with no photo or fact were deleted. Submit the pillars, cadence, brand voice, all four weeks and the owner's written approval.
mistakes: Accepting AI ideas that have no real product, photo or fact behind them.
Using customers' photos with no written permission recorded.
Planning a daily WhatsApp broadcast to everyone instead of at most weekly to opted-in customers.
A brand voice with no list of claims the agent must never make.
b.pass: Five pillars each fed by a named source, a cadence per platform, a one-page brand voice with banned claims, and a four-week calendar where every idea names its product, photo or fact, signed off by the owner.
b.redo: Send it back if ideas have no source, the WhatsApp plan ignores opt-in, or there is no owner approval.

s.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane on Facebook and Instagram, Telegram approval, five real posts.

  1. Draft (Fridays 14:00): read next week's Calendar rows → AI with the brand voice, idea, current price and last week's top posts → one object per platform (caption, hashtags, alt_text, uses_price).
  2. Check (Code): Instagram must have a public image or video URL; captions must avoid the brand voice's banned phrases; at most a few hashtags. Failures go back to the AI once, then to Tolu marked "needs edit".
  3. Approve: Telegram message per item with both versions and the photo; Approve, Edit, Skip. Approval stores price_at_approval.
  4. Publish (every 15 minutes): due and approved rows → check posting_paused → price re-check:
const live = $('Price list').all()
  .find(r => r.json.product === $json.product)?.json.price;
if ($json.uses_price && live !== $json.price_at_approval) {
  return { ...$json, status: 'held', reason: `price now ${live}` };
}
return { ...$json, status: 'go' };

Then Facebook: Graph API photo with message to the Page. Instagram: create the media container (public image URL and caption), then publish it. Save each post_id. Error workflow alerts Tolu on any failure.

mistakes: Sending an Instagram version with no image or video URL.
Using the price written into Friday's draft instead of re-reading the sheet at publish time.
No pause setting checked before publishing.
Not saving the returned post IDs, so the weekly report cannot fetch insights.
s.pass: Execution logs show five posts published at their scheduled times on two platforms with saved post IDs, every version passing its checks, and one post held when its price changed after approval.
s.redo: Send it back if a post went out without approval, a held-price test is missing, or any post was late or failed silently.

g.answer:
Worked example: Glow Studio, the fictional Enugu salon from Bronze, run for four weeks on Instagram, Facebook and TikTok (TikTok as drafts the owner posts in the app until the app is audited).

PillarPostsAvg reachEnquiries
Style of the week1264019
Behind the chair99106
Client transformations81,35023
Hair-care tips75202
Offers and dates578011

Cadence kept: 41 of 42 planned posts went out on time; one was paused on a national day of mourning using the pause switch.

Owner's time: 14, 12, 10 and 9 minutes in weeks 1 to 4 (Telegram timestamps).

Against the month before: posts 6 → 41; total reach about 3,100 → 33,000; enquiries by DM or call 22 → 61. Bookings were not tracked last month, so we compare enquiries only.

Changes each week

  1. Week 1 → 2: moved posts from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. after insights showed evening reach was higher.
  2. Week 2 → 3: one more transformation post, one fewer tip.
  3. Week 3 → 4: shorter TikTok videos (under 20 seconds) after watch time fell.
  4. Week 4: owner asked to keep the plan as it is for the next month.

Submit: the pillar table, the published post log with post IDs, insights screenshots for both months, the owner's minutes, and these weekly changes.
mistakes: Comparing with a 'month before' that has no measured numbers.
Promising the owner automated TikTok posting before the app is audited.
Reporting likes only, with no reach or enquiries.
Never changing the plan from week to week.
g.pass: Four weeks on at least three platforms on cadence, the owner's time under 15 minutes a week with evidence, results by pillar, one change per week, and reach or enquiries compared with the previous month.
g.redo: Send it back if the cadence broke without explanation, the owner spent more than 15 minutes a week, or there is no comparison with the month before.
